name: Democratic Republic of the Congo

findings.local_actor: SCPT (Société Congolaise des Postes et Télécommunications)
findings.summary: The national fibre backbone was built by Chinese state contractor CITCC with SCPT on China Eximbank loans: phase 1 Kinshasa–Muanda (650 km, completed 2010), phase 2 (3,300 km, US$221m) received final acceptance in October 2017.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole prc: no source names the original optical-equipment vendor; CITCC is a PRC state contractor, and 35Nord (2020) reports Huawei upgraded the SCPT backbone from 10G to 100G, making Huawei the current equipment supplier on one S3 source only. US$221m is phase 2 (Ecofin); phase 1 loan was RMB 245m (about US$42.5m per DRC Aid Management Platform, cited by AidData), subject of a parliamentary overpricing inquiry. Current operation not confirmed; still_current null.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Posts, Telecommunications and NTIC (PT-NTIC)
findings.summary: At the first E-DRC forum in Kinshasa, Huawei DRC and the telecoms ministry signed a memorandum of understanding on ICT cooperation, infrastructure deployment, rural coverage and Huawei input to the national digital plan.
findings.analyst_inference: Non-binding MOU (tier 1); no follow-on contract found in this run.

findings.local_actor: Ministry of Posts and Telecommunications, DRC
findings.summary: The DRC signed an MOU with Chinese firm Genew Technologies for a fibre network laid along the Congo River bed from Muanda to Kisangani (1,700 km plus 400 km junctions), announced at US$1.5bn; financing unclear, no construction reported.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1 (MOU only). Genew as equipment supplier is assumed to be the controller under the equipment rule; whether Genew would supply equipment or only build is not stated. First phase stated at over US$400m.

findings.summary: Raxio inaugurated a US$30m carrier-neutral Uptime Tier III colocation data centre in Limete, Kinshasa: 1,542 sq m, up to 400 racks, 1.5 MW IT load, described as the country's largest.
findings.analyst_inference: Pole null: neither opened source states Raxio Group's home jurisdiction or shareholders, so the controller's pole is unresolved. The 2021 source is the project announcement (planned Q2 2022 commissioning); the 2024 source reports inauguration, hence tier 5 on one source for operation.

findings.controller: Inga development agency (ADEPI), Government of DRC
findings.financier: World Bank (US$1bn commitment to Inga, not data-centre specific)
findings.summary: At a US–Congo investment forum in Washington, the head of Congo's Inga agency pitched the Inga hydro site to AI data-centre developers; no operator, investor or agreement was named, and an Inga law was still being drafted.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 1 statement of intent only. Date is the forum Wednesday inferred from a 16 October 2025 article; agency name ADEPI is analyst knowledge, the article says Inga development agency. World Bank financing is for Inga generally, not tied to any data centre.
